rules.title: Open API type: The API design meets the open type definition requirements.
rules.zh_summary: 开放 API 须按 x-api-type 明确标注为 open-api 或 inner-public-api 并在 API Gateway 注册；面向租户的开放 API 必须配套文档、API Explorer、SDK、CLI 与示例。

blocks.text: Open APIs are APIs that can be invoked by tenants or cloud services using tenant credentials. Such APIs are open to all scenarios and can be directly accessed by tenants. Open APIs must provide developer suites such as documents, API Explorer, SDK, CLI, and examples. In principle, the console can be built based on Open APIs.

Internal APIs are APIs that can be invoked by cloud services using the op account credentials, app codes credentials, or certificate two-way authentication credentials. Such APIs are used only after being authorized by the cloud service management zone. Tenants cannot access these APIs.

rules.title: Idempotent: API design must follow idempotent.
rules.zh_summary: 幂等要求：查询(GET)必须幂等、删除(DELETE)必须幂等、修改(PUT)与创建(POST)建议幂等——N 次相同请求与单次请求的副作用一致。
checks: GET 查询接口不改变资源状态（幂等）
DELETE 重复删除结果一致（幂等，不因已删除而报错或产生不同副作用）
PUT 全量更新接口幂等
POST 创建接口若支持幂等则具备去重/幂等键机制

blocks.text: Idempotence. In the HTTP/1.1 specification, idempotent is defined as follows:
Methods can also have the property of "idempotence" in that (aside from error or expiration issues) the side-effects of N > 0 identical requests is the same as for a single request.
By definition, the idempotent of an HTTP method means that a single and multiple requests for a resource should have the same side effects.
(1) The API(GET) for querying resources, Support for idempotency is required.
(2) The API(PUT) for modifying resources is recommended that idempotent be supported.
(3) The API(POST) for creating resources is difficult to implement idempotent, It is recommended to support idempotence.
(4) The API(Delete) for deleting resources is must that idempotent be supported.

rules.zh_summary: 单个 API 必须保证操作原子性；操作失败时须清理过程中产生的垃圾数据，不残留半成品资源。

blocks.text: Note: When resources or services become bottlenecks, the service needs to start the flow control protection mechanism to keep your your services still operable.

The public cloud API flow control is hierarchical. The service needs to provide the local flow control capability. When the threshold is exceeded, the service starts the local flow control. If the service provides external interfaces, the API-GW can perform outer flow control. The API-GW is responsible for outer flow control.
The service needs to provide the API flow control baseline value in typical scenarios.

blocks.text: Services that provide APIs for external systems need to provide the interface for querying and obtaining the API version number of the service (the get / interface is required). The interface must specify which version number is the recommended version and which versions are supported but not recommended. This API enables API users to quickly learn about and follow up the changes of service APIs.

The API version number is global information of the service and does not involve any resource operation. Therefore, token authentication is not required for the API. If get / or get/{version} is inherited from the open source community, the authentication policy must be the same as that in the community. In the preceding command, get/{version} is not mandatory.

blocks.text: For a single resource operation of a RESTful API, the HTTP verbs corresponding to the standard CRUD operation of a resource are as follows, which complies with the following rules:
[Rule] The GET operation is used to obtain list of resources or single resource.
[Rule] GET operations must be secure and idempotent.
Note: Both security and idempotence refer to the fact that the server resource state does not change after the operation.
[Rule] If the GET operation succeeds, the status code 200 (OK) is returned.

[Suggestion] (1) If the client has cached resources, add condition information such as If-Modified-Since to the header of a GET request. If the server detects that the resources are not changed, the server returns 304 (Not Modified). Notify the client that the cached consultation information can still be used.

(2) To standardize the return body format: The root node should use {} to facilitate expansion. Use the get method to query single resource information, the body should not use list format [], but rather {} format. When querying a resource list, the body should use list format []. Refer to example 2.7.4 for guidance.

(3) Exceptional Scenarios: POST can be used only when the request parameters have complex multi-level nested structures, the number of parameters is too large to exceed the URI length limit, or there is sensitive information that is not suitable to be placed in the Path and Query. In other cases, GET should be used.
[Rule] Applicable to create resource scenarios and scenarios where CRUD cannot express operations (Non-CRUD).
Note: For the application scenarios of operations that cannot be expressed by CRUD, see section "Non-CRUD Resources".
[Rule] If the resource is successfully created, the status code 201 (Created) is returned. Status code 200 (OK) is returned for the non-CRUD operation.

[Rule] If the operation URL is a new resource, create the resource, When creating resources, prioritize using POST. If the URL is an existing resource, update the resource. Some content can be updated.

Note: For example, PUT /users/admin indicates that if the user whose ID is admin does not exist, create a user whose ID is admin and set attributes for the user. If yes, the system updates the user information based on the input parameters.
[Rule] If the PUT command is used to create a resource successfully, the status code 201 (Created) is returned. If the resource is modified successfully, the status code 200 (OK) is returned.

[Rule] The message body transferred by the PUT operation must contain complete information about the resource to be replaced. If the transferred information is incomplete, the service implementation end only needs to replace the transferred value. If no value is provided for the parameter, the original value on the server is retained and the original value is not cleared. You cannot set default values for the parameters transferred by PUT. The existing behaviors of the inventory interface are retained based on the compatibility principle.
[Rule] The PATCH operation is used to update some resources.
[Rule] If a partial update operation is successful, the status code 200 (OK) is returned.
[Suggestion] If the size of the resource information required by the PUT operation is similar to that required by the PATCH operation, the PUT operation is preferred.

Note: RFC 5789 (PATCH Method for HTTP) clearly states that "PATCH is neither safe nor idempotent as defined by [RFC2616], Section9.1." indicates that the PATCH method is not idempotent. In addition, the PATCH method is not uniformly used in the industry, and most standard development frameworks do not fully support PATCH. Therefore, the PATCH operation is not recommended if the PUT request can be used to define operation interfaces. If some services must be used, you need to define the request body format and application scenario.
[Rule] The DELETE operation is used to delete resources.
[Rule] The DELETE operation must be idempotent.
[Rule] The DELETE operation should not include request body parameters.

[Rule] If the resource is deleted successfully, the status code 200 (OK) or 204 (No Content) is returned. If the service receives the request but does not perform the operation immediately, the status code 202 (Accepted) is returned.

blocks.text: The API for obtaining resource collections must support pagination.
The pagination parameters can be set as optional. You do not need to enter the parameters.

If the pagination parameter is optional, the service must set a default number of displayed records. Currently, the IaaS requires that the default number of displayed records is 1000. This description must be described in the API reference to prevent users from thinking that full information is queried. The use of other pagination parameters is prohibited.
The URL parameters used by the pagination request can be set in either of the following modes，Do not use other pagination parameters:
·marker: ID of the last record on the previous page.
·limit: number of entries displayed per page
indicates that a maximum of 100 records that meet the query conditions are displayed after 344bd0.
"page_info":{ "next_marker":"006f492b-xxxx" Return to Next page Query address
"previous_marker": "003e6eba-xxxx" Return to the query address of the previous page.
"current_count": 2 Number of returned items on this page
·offset: indicates the offset from which the query starts. The offset is greater than or equal to 0.
·limit: number of entries displayed per page
Indicates that a maximum of 100 records that meet the query conditions are displayed from the fourth record. When offset is set to 0, the first record is displayed.

Note: When the offset and limit paging modes are used, the performance may be affected when the records are too large. Therefore, the service scale must be considered. (For details, see the following: https://blog.novatec-gmbh.de/art-pagination-offset-vs-value-based-paging/ ).
If the original API is used as the start page of the pagination list, change the value to the offset in the new API version.

blocks.text: 3. Note: Open APIs use unified error code and return code coding rules.

Each service must define its own error code. Error codes with the same semantics must be the same for all services. An error code must correspond to the same error message. Error messages can support variables.
If the request fails, the application-level error code (error_code) and error description (error_msg) must be returned in the response body.

The error code must start with the service abbreviation +. + Error code in numeric coding mode. To ensure compatibility with existing APIs, the current number length can be 4-bit XXXX, 6-bit XXXX, or 8-bit XXXXXXX. If the preceding specifications are not met, rectification must be performed. In the future, the length of the digital code will be gradually unified to 8-bit with the version evolution.
When the request is successful, the response body does not contain the error code (error_code) and error description (error_msg).
In addition to the error_code and error_msg fields, the error response message can contain other fields defined by the product to facilitate fault locating. It reduces the complexity of client logic.
If an OpenAPI service that has interconnected with the new IAM 5.0 plane denies the user access due to lack of permission, the encoded_authorization_message field must be carried.
Depending on the downstream service error code:

In principle, services can return only the error code and error message of the service. If the error message of integrated third-party services needs to be returned, the error code and error message can be combined into the error message of the service and returned. The implementation details and confidential information should be hidden.
The extended error information is as follows:
If the current error consists of multiple errors or has a more specific cause, you are advised to use details to describe the more detailed error information. Application scenario:
Service error codes are split. To ensure compatibility, new error codes can be returned in details.

Error information about the downstream services that depend on must be returned. The returned information in details is the same as the service invoking sequence. For example, service A invokes service B, and service B invokes service C. The returned details of service A are integrated in the [B, C, ...] format. That is, the call error response information closest to service A must be at the beginning of the list.
